title: Covenant & Biblical Theology

sections.title: Covenant theology

questions.prompt: What best explains the unity of God’s saving dealings across biblical history?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: One covenant of grace is administered in different ways across the biblical covenants.

choices.label: B
choices.text: One saving purpose unfolds through distinct covenants and reaches its goal in the new covenant, without requiring one overarching covenant of grace.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Distinct divine administrations preserve significant differences in God’s dealings with Israel and the church.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I trace several interlocking promises without adopting a single organizing framework.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Was Adam in a covenant in which life was promised on condition of obedience?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes. A covenant of works or life links Adam’s obedience to the life of those he represents.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Adam had a covenantal calling, but I would not describe the promised outcome as earned by his works.

choices.label: C
choices.text: God gave Adam commands and consequences, but I would not infer a covenant of this kind.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: How does Christ’s obedience relate to Adam’s calling?
questions.displayNote: ↳ After COV-02, if A or B is selected.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Christ fulfills the obedience required of humanity as the last Adam.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Christ recapitulates and heals Adam’s failed vocation, but I would avoid describing it as fulfillment of the same covenantal condition.

choices.label: C
choices.text: I affirm the Adam–Christ parallel but do not derive a covenantal arrangement from it.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Was the new covenant already the saving reality enjoyed by believers before Christ’s coming?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes. Earlier believers shared in the same covenant of grace under earlier administrations.

choices.label: B
choices.text: They received the benefits of Christ’s future work by promise, while the new covenant itself was established in history by Christ.

choices.label: C
choices.text: I affirm that they were saved through God’s grace but avoid calling their covenant relationship the new covenant.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

introduction: An administration is a historical form in which God orders a covenant relationship.
editorialNotes: Distinguish a theological covenant inferred from Scripture from a covenant explicitly named in a passage.

furtherStudy.text: Westminster Confession, chapter VII, on covenant and its administrations.
Second London Baptist Confession, chapter VII, on the revelation of the covenant of grace.

sections.title: Dispensationalism

questions.prompt: When the New Testament describes a new administration in God’s plan, what changes?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: The terms under which God orders a community’s life change, while salvation is always by grace.

choices.label: B
choices.text: A new phase brings earlier covenant promises to fulfillment and transforms the identity or obligations of their recipients.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It is chiefly a change in the clarity or form of administration of one covenant of grace.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I need to judge each change separately and do not see one answer applying to every transition.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Is Christ’s present reign already a fulfillment of the promise of David’s throne?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes. That promise is being fulfilled in Christ’s present kingship.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Yes, in an inaugurated sense, with a further earthly fulfillment still expected.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Christ reigns now, but his specifically Davidic reign awaits a future fulfillment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Scripture establishes Christ’s kingship more clearly than the relationship between its present and future forms.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Distinguish the existence of historical stages from the specific claims of dispensational systems.

furtherStudy.text: Dallas Theological Seminary, Doctrinal Statement, article V. The dispensations are described as “stewardships by which God administers His purpose.”

sections.title: New Covenant theology

questions.prompt: Who belongs to the new covenant itself?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: All who are inwardly renewed and know the Lord.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Believers and their children can belong to its visible administration, even though inward renewal is not identical with outward membership.

choices.label: C
choices.text: People enter a real covenantal relationship through Christian initiation and may subsequently fall away.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I distinguish present participation from a future fulfillment for Israel and need to specify which is meant.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: In what sense has the Sinai covenant become obsolete?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: The covenant as a whole has reached its goal. Christians receive their obligations through Christ.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Its ceremonial and national forms have expired, while its moral law continues to bind as moral law.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its role in covenant administration has changed, but aspects remain especially significant for Jewish followers of Jesus.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I do not think “obsolete” means that Israel’s covenant with God has simply ended.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: When Jesus calls a commandment new, where does its authority for Christians lie?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: In Christ’s own authority as lawgiver of the new covenant.

choices.label: B
choices.text: In Christ’s authoritative exposition of the moral law already binding on humanity.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In both the continuing moral claim and its new pattern in Christ’s own life and love.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: Do not infer infant baptism from a covenant label. Ask who belongs to the new covenant and reuse SAC for the rite.

furtherStudy.text: A. Blake White, New Covenant Theology questions, §§1–3, on the new covenant and the law of Christ.
Peter Gentry and Stephen Wellum, Kingdom through Covenant, on progressive covenantalism.

sections.title: Israel and the Church

questions.prompt: How do gentile believers in Christ relate to the covenant people of Israel?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: They are grafted into one people of God while Israel retains a distinctive identity and calling.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Promises to Israel reach their fulfillment in Christ and the people united to him, without a separate covenant destiny for national Israel.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Israel and the church remain distinct recipients of promises even as both depend on God’s grace.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Gentile Christians share Israel’s blessings, while the enduring covenant with the Jewish people should be affirmed on its own terms.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Must the land promises to Abraham have a future territorial fulfillment for his physical descendants?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes. A particular territorial fulfillment remains promised.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Their fulfillment expands in Christ to the inheritance of the whole renewed creation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They were fulfilled in Israel’s history and need no further territorial fulfillment.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A historical fulfillment and a future territorial fulfillment can both belong to the promise.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I would leave the form of fulfillment open.

questions.prompt: What do you expect from Paul’s words about “all Israel” in Romans 11:26?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: A future large-scale turning of Jewish people to Christ.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The salvation of the full number of Jewish believers across history.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The salvation of the whole people of God, Jews and gentiles in Christ.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A divine saving purpose for Israel whose timing or manner Paul leaves mysterious.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

introduction: Distinguish a claim about the Jewish people from a claim about a modern state or government.
editorialNotes: Distinguish Jewish identity, covenant standing, land, and future conversion. None alone settles a present political judgment.

sections.title: Continuity of biblical law

questions.prompt: On what grounds can an Old Testament command bind a Christian today?
questions.displayNote: Foundational  |  On entry to this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: It expresses enduring moral law rooted in God’s character or creation.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Christ or his apostles reaffirm it as part of the law of Christ.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Its underlying justice still directs Christian judgment, though its ancient form may differ.

choices.label: D
choices.text: A command given in Torah remains binding unless Scripture gives reason for a change.

choices.label: E
choices.text: It continues to bind Jewish believers as a covenant vocation even where gentile believers have a different obligation.

choices.label: F
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: What force might Israel’s civil penalties have for present civil authorities?
questions.displayNote: ↳ After COV-12, if A or C or D is selected.

choices.label: A
choices.text: Their principles of justice remain instructive while the specific penalties belonged to Israel’s polity.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The specified penalties retain presumptive authority unless later revelation changes them.

choices.label: C
choices.text: They witness to God’s judgment but are not a pattern for contemporary civil penalties.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: If the apostles never repeat the command to leave gleanings for the poor, what obligation follows for a Christian grower?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: The specific agricultural practice remains binding where applicable.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The practice embodies an enduring obligation to provide for neighbors, whose form may vary.

choices.label: C
choices.text: It instructs Christian generosity through Israel’s example, while the obligation is grounded in Christ’s teaching.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I see a commendable practice here without deriving a duty for every grower.

choices.label: E
choices.text: I’m unsure.

questions.prompt: Does distinguishing moral, ceremonial, and civil laws determine which Mosaic commands bind Christians?
questions.displayNote: Common follow-up  |  All readers of this dimension

choices.label: A
choices.text: Yes, if the categories are applied with attention to the purpose of each law.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The categories help interpret a law, but fulfillment in Christ ultimately determines its present force.

choices.label: C
choices.text: I regard the Sinai law as a covenantal whole and would avoid using this division to carry some parts across directly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: I’m unsure.

editorialNotes: For Sabbath practice see WCP. Distinguish being instructed by a law from standing under its covenantal jurisdiction.

Enter at any dimension. In guided mode, begin with its opening question, continue through the main questions in the order shown, and insert a follow-up only when its stated answer matches. After the branch, resume with the next main question. A skipped answer or uncertainty opens no conditional branch unless specified.

Choose the closest single answer unless multiple selections are invited. On multiple-response questions, an uncertainty or “none” choice stands alone. Treat unresolved tensions as invitations to clarify.

vocabulary.definition: A binding relationship established by God, expressed through promises and sometimes obligations or signs.
A family of Christian frameworks that sees God’s covenants as organizing the unity and development of the biblical story.
In classic Reformed theology, God’s covenant with Adam, in which life was promised on condition of obedience.
In classic Reformed theology, God’s saving covenant with fallen humanity through Christ, administered in different ways across biblical history.
A family of frameworks that distinguishes administrations in God’s plan and typically gives Israel and the Church distinguishable roles.
A framework that stresses the new covenant’s distinctness and understands the Mosaic law’s authority for Christians through Christ and his teaching.
The covenant promised in Jeremiah and inaugurated through Jesus Christ, associated with forgiveness and God’s law written on the heart.
